title: Play
html:
Play is fun. Play isn’t completely unstructured it’s just a scenario where you get to create the rules. There aren’t “no rules “ there are just rules of nature or rules of space or time but you get to set them. Play means looking at the world with new eyes, an opportunity to engage in opposite world…see how you can create a different reality for the fun of it. Play means making something by accident. Like a discovery or a new tool or a new feature. Play requires vulnerability …you have to be fearless and know the consequences aren’t that big of a deal …it’s kind of like gambling. Depends on what you plan on winning I guess. I plan on winning fun or process. Play shouldn’t require tools you don’t know? I don’t know what tools have to do with it… I suppose you should play with new tools in order to learn them.

Play is the easiest way to learn. By calling it play you feel a certain level of acceptable experimentation. Because in play the consequences are low, and just valued on how much or little you want to interact with the scenario. Play is just for fun, it’s just to engage in feeling, there isn’t another value to extract from it. Doesn’t make you any richer…only helps your brain make connections. So, seems like a really good tool for coming up with work. Tapping into feelings first. Letting the mind wander …then you start to bump into reality and see if it works in reality as well. What’s reality?

title: Work is a game.
html:
When players become engrossed, time seems to stop. They might say they’re having fun, relaxing, or in the zone. We call this feeling “the play state.”

Work is a game. If you make it a game, then time kind of disappears.

Work can be fun. Why does it not feel like it? What are the differences between work and play? Where do we get lost, or bogged down. How can they be reimagined or altogether avoided.

In child development, we learned how to survive as an adult through play (being social, balance, teamwork, etc.). If play can influence how we eventually work and live, then working and living can be again influenced by play? If it works one way, it can work the other way, no?

Qualities of play (rewritten by me, for me)

1. Make your own decisions. The type of materials offered can help make more meaningful decisions. Open-ended materials can be used in many ways so we can decide for themselves how to use them. For example, Foam pieces, little wooden sticks, ribbon scraps, and other reusable resources are all open-ended materials that inspire creative thinking.

What this makes me think of at work: being told what to make, leaving no opportunity for exploration.

2. Intrinsically motivated. The impulse to play comes from a natural desire to understand the world. This play impulse is as strong as the desire for food or sleep. It is this intrinsic motivation that allows us to regulate our own feelings and desires in order to keep playing.

What this makes me think of at work: I still have the desire to understand the world and learn. I am very motivated to solve the problem, intrinsically. I think the exercises of design encourage learning and discovery. When the discovery is taken away from the exercise, it’s no longer motivating.

3. Immersion in the moment. In true play, we are so fully engaged that we lose awareness of our surroundings, time, and space. In this risk-free atmosphere where reality is suspended, we have the security and safety we need to experiment, try new ideas, and investigate the laws of nature.

What this makes me think of at work: Work is not made to feel risk free. But, the measurements are so weak, that there isn’t even a feeling of accomplishment other than “done.” The constant check-in’s on progress, the shifting of priorities, goals, scope and new stakeholders with opinions strips any chance of losing an awareness of time.

4. Play is spontaneous, not scripted. Often, play is totally unplanned. Other times, play is planned but we impulsively make a change. Someone changes their mind, or perhaps an idea does not cooperate. This sense of the unknown provides us with opportunities to develop flexibility in thinking and decision making, which is a vital life skill.

What this makes me think of at work: This happens, actually. When random things pop up and there is so little time that only one person, with their own agency, can bring it to the finish line. There is some freedom in the tight timeline.

5. Play is enjoyable. Play always has an emotional response attached to it. Without this emotional connection, the experience is simply an activity; it is not PLAY. Enjoyment is the direct result of engaging in play. It is FUN!

What this makes me think of at work: My emotional connections at work. What would I say my emotions are…frustration, paranoid, disgruntled, unappreciated. Sometimes I feel happy and satisfied, and often I feel lucky. I also feel intrigued and interested. I think that is the source of frustration—there are so many opportunities for discovery and either they aren’t made available to me or no one else sees them.

What this makes me think of at work: Meetings, the work environment, emails, lunch, alerts, Slack messages, all make work work.

Questions for later:

How do I make my work space active?

If "play" cannot be accomplished, how about directed play?

What increases the risks and makes this slightly dangerous?

How do I build a striped down format, leaving only the least amount of structure to begin?

What rules can I make to ensure a playful approach? What does it need to answer?

Is it time based?

"The opposite of Play is not work, it’s depression." Brian Sutton-Smith

References

Qualities of play

Play Institute

Peter Gray’s Blog #6 Qualities of Play that Make It Ideal for Acquiring Skills

Books

Free to Learn

title: What is work?
html:
WORK

Work keeps you alive. Work keeps the fear out. Work is the antidote. Work is all time.

Work is a sustainable routine. Not a routine that you can sustain, but one that sustains you. Work is what keeps you alive and well. Work makes sure your needs are met. The goal is to do it so well that it keeps you alive not just as a requirement, but spiritually as well. Pour yourself into the craft or the detail, try to be better at it than anyone else. Try at it so hard new meaning emerges. What can you learn from this? What can you learn from this if you do it over and over. How is it different each day? What happens if you change it 1 degree or 3. Experiment with it. Work hard enough to call it play.

I spent some time watching videos about how to do laundry better. What makes whites whiter? How does pressing a collar make a shirt look more expensive? Since I have to do laundry, I might as well make it interesting.

I don’t always strive to get better at work. I don’t always turn labor into a game or a goal to reach. Even with proof that it improves when I do. When I was a bank teller in college, I decided to test my abilities with people, see what reactions I could manipulate. I watched people, picked up on patterns and learned more about my own patterns. People would storm in, furious over an overdraft fee and instead of reacting to their rage, I saw an experiment. I don’t remember exactly what I did, but my energy was probably more inviting than is normal. I nodded, I came along with them on their stories, I was calm, I listened. They weren’t screaming at me they were screaming at the problem. It worked! They always apologized to me. This was probably the first job that I realized my capacity for power (and love).

My father said “hobbies can you get through just about anything.” He also meant working at something, anything. When I was in high school he was learning to hunt with a bow and arrow. Then he learned how to golf. Now, at 82, he drives around in his ATV trimming the forest, making paths, and clearings, burning all the brush, drying wood. Work is a way to control the mind by giving it something to do. Work keeps the mind from being alone with, and then defined by thoughts— getting lost, overwhelmed and scared.

PLAY

The best way to have fun, is to not attach time to it. This is the problem with work. It could be fun, but the clock has a choke hold on the individual and the group. I have told my co-workers to get on board with the systems our team is making so that we can attain the ultimate goal: going home. It’s a race to leisure! Unbind from the clock!

Scientist have discovered that it takes approximately 400 repetiions to create and new synapse in the brain, unless it is done in play, which case it only takes 10 to 20 repetitions. (This link is not a real source)

I’m realizing now that I love productivity, and play is a very good strategy for getting work done, letting go, having fun while still presenting a challenge. Work is a game. If you make it a game, then time kind of disappears. Now I must look for more avenues to make time disappear.
